Specimen description: Karyotype study for the received POC (product of conception) sample was not possible as the  short  and  long  planned  cultures  did  not  yield  any  metaphases for the analysis. Hence the sample was processed for FISH (Fluorescence in situ Hybridization) study.

FISH  is  used  to  quickly  rule  out  the  most  common  chromosomal abnormalities  i.e.  Trisomy  13,  18,  21  and numerical  sex  chromosome  disorders  within  2-3  days.  The accuracy of this test is about 99%.

 

Clinical History : Missed abortion
Investigation  : Aneuploidy detection of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y

Method                                  

: Fluorescence in situ Hybridization (FISH)

Probes used

: Zytolight probe kit for chromosome 13, 18, 21, X and Y.

 2 Green, 2 Aqua (Blue) and 2 Orange signals show normal diploid status for chromosome 13, 18 and 21

RESULT: Normal for chromosomes 13, 18, 21 and sex chromosomes.

INTERPRETATION: No numerical abnormality found for chromosomes 13, 18, 21 and sex chromosomes.

LIMITATIONS OF FISH: Results can vary with respect to low grade mosaicism, maternal cell contamination, confined placental mosaicism, structural abnormalities like translocations, rearrangements involving centromeres, deletions and abnormalities of other chromosomes cannot be ruled out by FISH. Karyotyping should be carried out for this.
